PRIMARY CARE NOTE   Date: 2026-09-13
58F, ambulatory visit for an eye examination with primary care review.

S:
Patient presents for a routine ophthalmic examination and general review. She reports stable vision with no new floaters or blurring and feels generally well. She takes her blood pressure medication daily and monitors readings at home. Mild evening ankle swelling over the past few weeks prompted a cardiac screen today. No shortness of breath. She works as an accountant. Sister with schizophrenia. Appetite is good; diet includes frequent sugary drinks, which were discussed. Lives with her spouse. Never smoker, rare alcohol.

O:
BP 124/76, HR 70, RR 14, Temp 98.1 F, SpO2 98% on room air. Weight 160 lb, BMI 26.
General: well appearing, in no distress.
Eyes: visual acuity stable, conjunctivae clear, fundoscopic exam without hemorrhage or exudate.
CV: regular rate and rhythm, no murmur.
Lungs: clear to auscultation bilaterally.
Extremities: trace ankle edema, improves with elevation.
Labs (this week): A1c 7.1%, creatinine 1.1 mg/dL, eGFR stable post-transplant, BNP 42 pg/mL.

A/P:
1. Essential hypertension, well controlled on current regimen. Continue current antihypertensive. Home readings reviewed, averaging 122/76. Repeat basic metabolic panel in 12 months.
2. History of chronic kidney disease stage 4, resolved after kidney transplant. Graft function stable; continue immunosuppression as directed by the transplant team. Labs reviewed and acceptable.
3. R/o CHF; BNP normal. Ankle swelling is mild, improves overnight, and fits long hours seated at her desk; no echocardiogram needed. Advised leg elevation in the evenings and short walking breaks at work.
4. Type 2 diabetes mellitus without complications, A1c 7.1%. Continue metformin 500 mg twice daily. Reviewed reducing sugary drinks and adding daily walks. Recheck A1c in 3 months.
5. Eye care: dilated exam without acute findings. Continue annual dilated eye examinations.

Return in 3 months for routine follow-up, sooner for worsening swelling.
